newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic begins trials for device.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic begins trials for device.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said Thursday it is beginning U.S. clinical testing of an implantable device designed to detect and treat a variety of heart rhythm disturbances including atrial and ventricular fibrillation.
Following approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, two implants were done Wednesday, one at the Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minn., and a second at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, Los Angeles.
Both patients are doing well and their physicians expect to discharge them from hospitals this week, Medtronic said in a news release.
About 70 patients have been enrolled in European clinical evaluations of the Jewel AF arrhythmia management device.
The Medtronic Jewel AF arrhythmia management device is one of the smallest and lightest defibrillators.

Medtronic estimates that more than 300,000 people worldwide are diagnosed each year with ventricular tachyarrhythmias and that about half are considered candidates for implantable device therapies. It is further estimated that 20 percent of these candidates also have atrial fibrillation, which is associated with a fivefold increase in the risk of stroke.

Atrial fibrillation affects about five million people worldwide and about two million in the United States, with about 720,000 new patients diagnosed each year worldwide. Medtronic estimates that about 100,000 may be candidates for an implantable arrhythmia management device.
Medtronic, a medical technology company, specializes in implantable and interventional therapies.
